title: Milo's bet: every planet in 90 seconds
note: Loop-Ende: Der letzte Satz ('...still can't believe that on Venus,') führt direkt in den ersten Satz.

scenes.text: one day lasts longer than a whole year. Milo said that to his boss, and got laughed out of the room.
Wait, what? Yep. One spin of Venus takes 243 Earth days. One lap around the Sun? Only 225. So Milo makes a bet. He'll fly to every planet, and every single one will be even weirder.
First stop, the Sun. It's 4.6 billion years old, and it holds 99.8 percent of all the mass in the solar system. Everything else? Crumbs.
Mercury races around the Sun in just 88 days. Milo does the math. A birthday every three months. He is thrilled.
Then Venus. Not the closest planet, but the hottest. 467 degrees Celsius. Hot enough to melt lead, because its thick air traps the heat like a greenhouse. And the Sun? It rises in the west.
Back past Earth, 150 million kilometers from the Sun. The light on your face right now left the Sun about eight minutes ago.
On Mars, Milo finds Olympus Mons, the biggest volcano in the whole solar system. Next to it, Mount Everest is basically a speed bump.
Jupiter is so huge that if it were hollow, about 1,000 Earths could fit inside.
Saturn's rings look smooth, right? Nope. Billions of chunks of ice and rock, some as big as a house.
Uranus is tilted almost 98 degrees. It literally rolls around the Sun on its side.
And Neptune? Winds over 2,000 kilometers per hour. One year there lasts about 165 Earth years, so you'd never even reach your first birthday.
Milo wins the bet. So, real talk, which planet would you pick? Tell me in the comments. Because his boss still can't believe that on Venus,
